cards_stock.narrative: The debit card market has stabilised after the Apr 2026 purge — the base expanded 45 lakh cards to 103 crore in May 2026, the first growth in two months, confirming the 2.14 crore Apr 2026 contraction was a one-time cleanup of inactive cards. YoY growth held flat at 2.75% for two consecutive months, the first time the rate has been unchanged, signaling the market has reached a new equilibrium at a lower structural growth rate than the 2025 baseline. Private banks reached their highest debit share on record at 25.88%, while PSBs fell 0.21pp to 63.97%, confirming the Apr 2026 surge to 64.17% was a temporary rebalancing event. Payment banks stabilised at 6.1%, up 0.1pp from the Apr 2026 trough, and the issuance-spend gap widened 1.3pp to 7.1pp, still in the lower range of the 17-period distribution. The market is expanding again, but at a slower pace than 2025, and concentration is easing as mid-tier banks recover.
